synthesis_notes: The provided literature set is overwhelmingly non-relevant to the proton-transport mechanism hypotheses, so it places only very weak constraints on H1–H4. Most cards concern unrelated biological, electronic, or materials topics and therefore leave all four hypotheses unresolved. The only partially relevant papers are the zwitterionic hydrogel/elastomer studies and the plant freezing-tolerance paper, which broadly support the plausibility that low-temperature behavior in hydrated ionic or zwitterionic networks can be governed by nonuniform water binding, antifreezing interfacial solvation, and residual mobility in strongly associated domains. That general pattern is more consistent with mechanisms invoking heterogeneous populations or interfacial residual pathways—thus giving weak qualitative support to H1, H2, and H4 over a fully single-population picture like H3—but these papers do not directly probe phosphoric-acid/water proton transport, distinguish sequential freezing from percolation loss, or establish a surface-hopping handoff. Overall, the literature picture is that there is no direct mechanistic evidence here to decisively support or weaken any hypothesis, aside from a slight heuristic tilt toward heterogeneous/interfacial explanations rather than a single confined population with only dynamical crossovers.
